text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel ready to promise no establishment of new settlements during peace negotiations.
- Charge sheet: Israeli businessman sold nerve gas and mustard gas to Iran.
- U.S. to Israel: End laundering of drug money.
- Eisenberg daughter says she deserves half of the fortune.
- Treasury weighs nationalising all sick funds.
- Superviser of Banks says strengthening of dollar will cause repayment problems for banks.
- Strauss expected to get go-ahead to acquire Elite.
- Wave of senior managers leaving Bezeq.
MAARIV
- Israeli businessman supplied Iran with materials for chemical weapons for money.

- Tension in Israel-Jordan relations; surprise cancellation of secret meeting between Israeli Infrastructure Minister Sharon and Jordanians on water; Jordanian Crown Prince Hassan will not participate in ceremony today with Netanyahu.
- Today meeting between Israeli President Weizman and Palestinian President Arafat.
- Strauss will pay $61.5 million for Elite control.
- AT&T holds up payment of $10 million to Bezeq.
HAARETZ
- Crisis in water talks with Jordan; Prince Hassan cancels meeting with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu.
- Prosecution: Israeli businessman got $16 million from Iran for material to make chemical weapons.
- Member of Third Way party to Netanyahu: If we leave government you won't be able to depend on ultra-religious and ignoramuses.
- Ministry of Religion readies to set up area for Jewish worshippers at section of Western Wall in Moslem Quarter.
- Public commission to recommend limiting members' of parliament immunity.
- Coca-Cola declared monopoly in carbonated drink sector.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israel to offer Palestinian Authority gestures including large-scale construction for Palestinians including in Jerusalem and flexibility on Gaza airport.
- Israeli army, U.S. and Turkey finalise details for joint naval exercise, likely this summer in Mediterranean.
- Palestinian Authority introduces death penalty for selling land to Israelis.
- Hamas political leader Marzuk arrives in Jordan after release from U.S. jail.
- Treasury says no firm figure for budget cut.
- Lack of funds puts Railway 2000 project in doubt.
- Cellcom cellular phone company recommends using headsets to cut health risks.
GLOBES
- Eisenberg 1975 will, as opposed to 1986 version, gave half of estate to his widow and daughters.
